fixed.problem: Review blocking 1 (W8-host-2, never cut): the paged ETag read missed an item added after an exactly full last page and reported that nothing had changed. When a status issue held a multiple of 100 comments, the other Forerunner's next announcement stayed invisible to the poller. Root cause (github.ts pagedConditional, was :470): a page answered 304 was served from the copy together with the copy's Link header. GitHub's ETag, and the stand-in's, covers the page body only, so a full last page keeps its ETag. The old Link named no next page, so the read stopped there and the joined ETag still matched the caller's.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/capabilities/test/githost-issues.test.ts, describe "w8-issue-host, wave 8: a paged read with the ETag past an exactly full last page (W8-host-2, http)": all 3 cases failed before the fix. (1) A page of 3: the 4th and 7th comments, a removed 7th, and a quiet poll that costs no rate-limit point once the page after is a 304. (2) The default page of 100: the 101st comment. (3) Issues listed oldest first: the 4th issue. Also the fetch-stub case "fixup-w8-issue-host: a full last page answered from the copy under a cursor next link is read again in full ...", which failed before.
fixed.how: A page answered from the copy is no longer taken as the end of the list when it is full (as many items as its per_page) and has no next link. On a numbered list the adapter also reads the page after it (page + 1). That read is conditional, so it costs a rate-limit point only the first time; after that it is a free 304. The page after joins the result and its ETag only when it holds items. Under a cursor link (after, before or cursor), where there is no page number, the adapter reads the full page again without If-None-Match and follows the fresh Link. conditionalGet gained {fresh}; the module-private helpers are fullPage and numberedPageAfter. listIssueComments and listIssues both go through this path. The capabilities.md sentence 'it changes when any page changes' is replaced with the real rule.

fixed.problem: Review non-blocking: pinIssue read the issue (for its node id) outside its refusal handling. A 401 or 403 on that read threw provider_auth or tool_not_allowed where the port promises 'forbidden'. The re-read of the pins after GitHub refuses a pin as UNPROCESSABLE (three pins taken in a race) was never reached by any test.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/capabilities/test/githost-issues.test.ts, "fixup-w8-issue-host: pinning answers forbidden when the issue's own read is refused, and reads the pins again when GitHub refuses the pin as unprocessable". Before the fix it threw 'GET /repos/o/r/issues/7 -> 401: no'.
fixed.how: getIssue now runs inside pinIssue's try, so 401 and 403 answer 'forbidden' and nothing is sent to GraphQL. A missing issue still throws not_found. The new fetch-stub case covers the race: the re-read gives 'limit' when three are pinned, 'pinned' when this issue is one of them, and otherwise the validation refusal stands. capabilities.md now says the same.
fixed.check_in_the_app: No screen changes. Live (final_check F-W8-1): pinIssue with a token that cannot read the sandbox repository answers 'forbidden', not an error. A fourth pinIssue answers 'limit' and unpins nothing.

fixed.problem: Review non-blocking, a stand-in fidelity regression from w8-issue-host: HostStore.affiliations(login, 'write') now leaves out organisations whose base permission is read, and canCreateRepo uses those affiliations. As a result, a member of a read-base organisation could no longer create a repository in it. On GitHub that is a separate member privilege and it is on by default.
fixed.failing_test_before: testenv/test/githost.test.ts, "fixup-w8-issue-host: a member of an organisation whose base permission is read still creates a repository in it, as GitHub's default member privilege allows; a stranger cannot". Before the fix it got 404 instead of 201.
fixed.how: testenv/src/githost/auth.ts canCreateRepo also accepts the subject's readOrgs; a stranger still gets 404. docs/maintainers/testing.md now says so.

not_done.problem: Review non-blocking: the 404-as-no_permission probe exists only on createIssue. A 404 from commentOnIssue or updateIssueComment in a repository the token can see reads as 'missing'.
not_done.why: Left as it is, on purpose. On those two routes a 404 can be a deleted issue or comment, and one GET of the repository cannot tell that apart from missing access. Adding the probe there would turn a gone comment into 'no permission'. GitHub usually answers 403 for missing access, and that already reads as no_permission. The note for w8-status-write is in notes_for_other_areas.

not_done.problem: Review non-blocking: conditionalGet reads the vault token for the cache key, and request() reads it again, so a token replaced between the two reads is stored under the old token's key.
not_done.why: Not changed. The window is two awaits wide, and both tokens are the same person's vault token. The next read with the new token misses the cache and is a full 200. Closing it would mean passing explicit headers through request(), a wider change to a shared transport than this fix-up needs.

not_done.problem: Review non-blocking (pre-existing): GET /repos/:o/:r/issues/comments (the repository-wide list) is shadowed by /issues/:number on the stand-in, and repoJson's permissions.admin is too loose for collaborators.
not_done.why: Both predate this area, and nothing uses them yet. They are listed in new_problems for w8-shared-repo and whichever later area first reads the repository-wide list.

notes_for_other_areas: w8-status-read / w8-github-feed: pagedConditional (github.ts) now reads the page after a full last page that was answered from the copy (page + 1, conditional: one rate-limit point the first time, a free 304 after that). Under a cursor Link it re-reads the full page without If-None-Match, which costs one rate-limit point per poll while the list sits exactly at a page boundary. The joined ETag includes the page after only when that page holds items. notModified from listIssueComments now holds at every page boundary. Moving listPullRequests onto pagedConditional (w8-github-feed) gets this behaviour with no further change.

w8-status-write: a 404 from commentOnIssue or updateIssueComment reads as 'missing' (issueRefusalOf), never as 'no_permission'. On those routes a 404 can be a deleted issue or comment. When the status comment or issue was read a moment before, treat 'missing' as 'gone or no longer reachable' and re-read before writing again. createIssue alone probes the repository and marks no_permission.
pinIssue now answers 'forbidden' for a 401 or 403 on any of its reads, the issue's own read included. A missing issue still throws not_found.
Stand-in: any member of an organisation may create a repository in it, whatever the base permission (canCreateRepo accepts readOrgs).
